answers: The point $(-2,-3)$ corresponds to $-2-3i$, with modulus $\sqrt{(-2)^2+(-3)^2}=\sqrt{13}$.

questions.q: Solve $x^2+2x+5=0$, giving your answer in the form $a+bi$.
One root of a quadratic equation with real coefficients is $3-4i$. State the other root, and find the quadratic equation.
questions.answer: Since the coefficients are real, complex roots occur in conjugate pairs, so the other root is $3+4i$. Sum of roots $=6$; product $=(3-4i)(3+4i)=9+16=25$. Equation: $x^2-6x+25=0$.

questions.q: Given that $z=1+2i$ is a root of $z^3-4z^2+9z-10=0$ (with real coefficients), find the other two roots.
questions.answer: Since the coefficients are real, $z=1-2i$ is also a root. These two roots multiply to $(1+2i)(1-2i)=1+4=5$ and sum to $2$, giving the quadratic factor $z^2-2z+5$. Dividing the cubic by this factor: $z^3-4z^2+9z-10\div(z^2-2z+5)=z-2$, so the third root is $z=2$. The other two roots are $1-2i$ and $2$.

sections.heading: Multiplying and dividing in polar form

questions.q: Given $z_1=4\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ and $z_2=2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{12}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)$, find $z_1z_2$ and $\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}$ in polar form.
questions.answer: Multiply moduli, add arguments: $z_1z_2=8\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{12}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{12}\right)$. Divide moduli, subtract arguments: $\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}=2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

questions.q: Given $z_1=5\left(\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{5}+i\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)$ and $z_2=\cos\dfrac{\pi}{5}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{5}$, find $z_1z_2$ and $\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}$ in polar form.
Find the modulus and argument of $z=\dfrac{(1+i)^3}{1-i}$, using De Moivre's theorem for the numerator and polar division.
questions.answer: $1+i$ has modulus $\sqrt{2}$ and argument $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, so $(1+i)^3$ has modulus $2\sqrt{2}$ and argument $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$. $1-i$ has modulus $\sqrt{2}$ and argument $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. Dividing: modulus $=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}=2$; argument $=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}-\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\pi$. (This means $z=-2$, purely real.)

sections.heading: Finding roots using De Moivre's theorem

questions.q: Find the three cube roots of $z=27\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, giving arguments in $[0,2\pi)$.
questions.answer: Cube roots have modulus $27^{1/3}=3$ and arguments $\dfrac{\pi/2+2\pi k}{3}$ for $k=0,1,2$: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$, $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$. Roots: $3\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$, $3\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)$, $3\left(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$.

questions.q: Find all four fourth roots of $-16$ (i.e. solve $z^4=-16$), giving arguments in $[0,2\pi)$.
questions.answer: Write $-16=16(\cos\pi+i\sin\pi)$. Fourth roots have modulus $16^{1/4}=2$ and arguments $\dfrac{\pi+2\pi k}{4}$ for $k=0,1,2,3$: $\dfrac{\pi}{4},\dfrac{3\pi}{4},\dfrac{5\pi}{4},\dfrac{7\pi}{4}$. Roots: $2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, $2\left(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)$, $2\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{4}\right)$, $2\left(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: AC circuit impedance

questions.q: This question has three parts. An AC circuit has impedance $Z=R+iX_L$, where $R=8\,\Omega$ (resistance) and $X_L=6\,\Omega$ (inductive reactance). (a) Write $Z$ in Cartesian form, find $|Z|$, and find $\arg Z$ to the nearest degree. (b) The current is $I=\dfrac{V}{Z}$, where $V=100$ volts (real). Find $I$ in the form $a+bi$, by rationalizing the denominator. (c) Find $|I|$, to two decimal places.
